title: From a Booking to the Day's Work
imageAlt: LodgeOps operations board showing arrivals, departures and tasks for a fictional sample lodge.
excerpt: Follow a stay from the room calendar into arrival planning, activities and crew assignments.

blocks.text: A reservation is more than a line on a calendar. The rooms, guests, services and dates saved on a LodgeOps booking give the team a starting point for the work that follows.
Start with the stay

Staff can begin a booking from an empty room and date on the Places calendar, or use New Booking on a narrow screen. The form collects the guest, party size, nights, room assignment and purchased services. Charges then show the stay and services together.
Turn a purchased activity into a plan

Buying a service creates an order on the booking; it does not silently assign a guide, equipment or time. An unscheduled activity appears in the day's Operations planning tasks. Staff choose a start time and concrete resources before saving the schedule.
The Crew and Assets calendars then show those commitments. Reopening the booking shows its assignments and preparation notes. Scheduling that already-purchased service does not charge it again.
Give each role the right view

Operations brings the day's guest flow and tasks together. Navigation and actions are matched to staff capabilities, with the API enforcing workspace and property access independently. The screen shown here uses a fictional sample lodge.

title: Planning Guides and Equipment for Activities
imageAlt: LodgeOps Crew calendar with scheduled guide assignments for a fictional sample lodge.
excerpt: See how purchased services become timed work with a guide, equipment and capacity checks.

blocks.text: A guest may buy a guided activity before anyone knows which guide or boat will be available. LodgeOps keeps the purchase on the booking, then lets staff schedule the actual work when the plan is ready.
Assign real resources

From Operations, a booking's Activities tab or an empty Crew or Assets calendar cell, staff can set the activity start, select a guide, optionally assign equipment and add preparation notes. The saved activity appears against the booking and the reserved resources.
Check the schedule before committing

Scheduling checks overlaps and capacity for the selected guide and asset. This helps staff avoid assigning the same resource to conflicting work. The Crew and Assets calendars give separate views of those commitments.
Shared sessions and pooled capacity are not part of the current workflow. Each scheduled activity uses concrete assignments. The calendar pictured here contains fictional sample lodge data.

title: From a Guest Tab to a Kitchen Ticket
imageAlt: LodgeOps kitchen ticket queue with preparing and ready orders for a fictional sample lodge.
excerpt: Record an extra on the booking and route prepared items to the kitchen without charging twice.

blocks.text: When a guest orders a meal or an extra, the sale and the preparation work should stay connected to their stay. LodgeOps starts that flow by selecting the booking in POS.
Set up products and stations

An operator creates stores and product groups, prices products in Settings and maps prepared items to a station in Kitchen configuration. A product without a station posts financially but does not create a preparation ticket.
Add the purchase to the right booking

Staff select the booking and store, optionally choose a guest in the party, and add the item with quantity and instructions. Add to tab records the purchase on the booking folio. For routed products it creates a kitchen or bar ticket too.
The ticket shows the room, guest, items, instructions and dietary information. Kitchen staff move it through preparing, ready and served. Those steps do not charge the guest a second time.
Handle included meals separately

Included meals can be planned by date, booking, meal and portions, then sent to the kitchen. Consuming that entitlement does not add a duplicate charge. The screen shown here uses a fictional sample lodge.

title: Following Charges, Payments and Reports
imageAlt: LodgeOps booking charges and balance for a fictional sample lodge.
excerpt: Keep the booking balance visible, record money received and read reports in each currency.

blocks.text: The booking folio is the place to review the stay, purchased services, extras and payments together. Staff can add a catalog or custom charge, review tax, and record money already received by cash, bank transfer, external terminal or another manual method.
Keep a traceable booking balance

Charges, payment history and the balance remain on the booking after reload. Allocations and reversals are part of the recorded financial history, so correcting a past entry does not require hiding the original.
Read reports with the right context

LodgeOps provides currency-specific finance views, allocation-backed overdue amounts, arrivals and departures, recorded-cost contribution and guest statistics. Screen and export cohorts are aligned. Occupancy uses current room inventory and recorded blocks; it is not a reconstruction of past inventory.

Provider payment links require separate setup and acceptance in the operating environment. A manually recorded payment does not prove a hosted checkout or bank settlement. The pictured booking belongs to a fictional sample lodge.
